{{Short description|none}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=April 2022}}
The top tier in English football today is the [[Premier League]], replacing the [[Football League First Division]] for the [[1992–93 FA Premier League|1992–93]] inaugural campaign. Since the [[1888–89 Football League|1888–89 season]], the first year of top flight football, three players have scored over 300 goals, with a further 25 players scoring over 200. In total, 256 players have scored 100 goals or more in the English top flight.<ref name=Free-elements-history/>

110 individual players have been named a season's top scorer. Players from [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]] have been top scorer more than any other club, appearing thirteen times on this list. [[Jimmy Greaves]], the all-time leading goalscorer in English top flight history, earned the accolade four times whilst at Tottenham. Nineteen nationalities are represented, and although the vast majority of top scorers have historically been English, there were fifteen times where the top scorer in the First Division was Scottish. Since the start of the Premier League era, the player (or players) that scores the most goals in a season is awarded the [[Premier League Golden Boot|Golden Boot]]. In the Premier League era, [[Thierry Henry]] of [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]] and [[Mohamed Salah]] of [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] have both won the Golden Boot on a record four occasions.<ref name=":9">{{cite news |title=Premier League Golden Boot award winners |url=http://www.premierleague.com/news/1206108 |access-date=22 September 2022 |publisher=Premier League}}</ref> Despite being the Premier League's third-highest goalscorer, [[Wayne Rooney]] does not appear on this list at all, having never finished an individual season as the top scorer.

Once a rarity, a more widespread assortment of nationalities has achieved this success in recent years; in the [[2018–19 Premier League|2018–19 season]], the Golden Boot was shared between three players from different African countries, and in the [[2021–22 Premier League|2021–22 season]], South Korean [[Son Heung-min]] finished level with Egypt's Mohamed Salah, becoming the first Asian to be named top scorer. [[Sergio Agüero]] won the award once, scoring 26 goals in the [[2014–15 Premier League|2014–15 season]]; in total, the Argentinian striker scored 184 goals between 2011 and 2021 to become the highest scoring foreign player in the top flight, a record later bettered by Salah during the [[2024–25 Premier League|2024–25 season]].<ref>{{cite web |author1=Ed McCambridge |date=7 March 2023 |title=Ranked! The Premier League's all-time foreign top scorers |url=https://www.fourfourtwo.com/features/ranked-the-premier-leagues-all-time-foreign-top-scorers |access-date=3 May 2023 |website=FourFourTwo}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |date=8 March 2025 |title=Mohamed Salah equals Premier League all-time record in Liverpool masterclass vs. Southampton |url=https://worldsoccertalk.com/news/mohamed-salah-equals-premier-league-all-time-record-in-liverpool-masterclass-vs-southampton/ |access-date=9 March 2025 |website=World Soccer Talk}}</ref>

==Top scorers==

===By season===
[[File:Jorge Robledo - Estadio 368.jpg|thumb|256x256px|[[George Robledo|Jorge Robledo]] was the first foreign player to score the most goals in a season, 33 for [[Newcastle United F.C.|Newcastle United]] in the 1951&ndash;52 season.]]
On six occasions [[Jimmy Greaves]] was the league top scorer: twice with [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]] and later four with [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]]; however, [[Steve Bloomer]] holds the record for one team, with five won with [[Derby County F.C.|Derby County]].<ref name=":0" /> [[Thierry Henry]] and [[Mohamed Salah]] are the record [[Premier League]] winners with four each. [[Gary Lineker]] has won the honour three times, all with different clubs, the only player to do so.

In the 1951–52 season, [[Chile national football team|Chile]] international [[George Robledo|Jorge 'George' Robledo]] became the first foreign player to score the most goals in a season, topping the list with 33 goals for [[Newcastle United F.C.|Newcastle United]].<ref name=":8">{{cite web |title=George Robledo - The First Foreign Golden Boot |url=https://thesporting.blog/blog/george-robledo-the-first-foreign-golden-boot |access-date=15 September 2022 |website=The Sporting Blog}}</ref> For two consecutive years the award was won by the lowest total of goals ever, 18.<ref name=":2" /> Englishmen [[Michael Owen]], [[Dion Dublin]] and [[Chris Sutton]] won in the [[1997–98 FA Premier League|1997–98 season]].<ref name=":3">{{cite web |title=Top Flight Highest Scorers 1888-89 to 2021-22 |url=https://www.myfootballfacts.com/premier-league/all-time-premier-league/top_flight_highest_goalscorers/ |access-date=15 September 2022 |website=My Football Facts}}</ref> Owen again won in the [[1998–99 FA Premier League|1998–99 season]],<ref name=":3" /> but this time he was joined by Dutchman [[Jimmy Floyd Hasselbaink]] and [[Dwight Yorke]],<ref name=":3" /> Trinidad and Tobago, the duo becoming the first foreign, league top scorers since Robledo. During this period however, two [[Republic of Ireland]] internationals, winger [[Andy McEvoy]] and striker [[John Aldridge]], topped the scoring charts. McEvoy shared the most goals with Jimmy Greaves in the [[1964–65 Football League|1964–65 season]] while Aldridge top scored for Liverpool in the [[1987–88 Football League|1987–88 season]]. Both players, although non-British, do not appear on the top foreign goalscorers list published by the [[International Federation of Football History & Statistics|IFFHS]]<ref name=":17">{{cite web |title=IFFHS |url=https://iffhs.com/en/news/erling-haalands-record-2703 |access-date=27 April 2023 |website=IFFHS}}</ref> as well as many other more reputable football websites. [[Didier Drogba]] (Ivory Coast) became the first African to win the award in [[2006–07 FA Premier League|2006–07 season]]<ref name=":3" /> and later [[Carlos Tevez]], [[Luis Suárez (Uruguayan footballer)|Luis Suárez]] and [[Sergio Agüero]] would add to the South American winners.<ref name=":3" /> In [[2018–19 Premier League|2018–19]], two players from the same club both finished as top scorers for the first time: [[Sadio Mané]] (Senegal) and Mohamed Salah (Egypt) of [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]],<ref>{{cite web |last=Ross |first=James M. |date=2 September 2021 |title=English League Leading Goalscorers |url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablese/engtops.html |access-date=18 September 2021 |work=[[RSSSF]]}}</ref> finished in another three way tie, joined by [[Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang]] (Gabon). The [[2021–22 Premier League|2021–22]] season saw [[Son Heung-min]] become the first Asian winner; the [[South Korea national football team|South Korean international]] scored 23 goals, finishing level with Mohamed Salah.<ref name=":2" />

From the start of the Premier League, a [[Premier League Golden Boot|Golden Boot]] trophy is presented to the top goalscorer. The first player to win this trophy was [[Teddy Sheringham]],<ref name=":3" /> then playing for [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]]. In the [[1993–94 FA Premier League|1993–94]] season [[Andy Cole]] scored 34 goals for Newcastle United, the highest number of goals in the Premier League era to win the award.<ref name=":2" /> The following season [[Alan Shearer]] equalled it while playing for Blackburn Rovers. Both these records however, were set during a 42-match season. Since the Premier League was reduced down to 20 teams, Mohamed Salah held the record previously with 32 in a 38-match season for [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] until [[Norway national football team|Norwegian]] striker [[Erling Haaland]] scored his 33rd goal for [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]] during the [[2022–23 Premier League|2022–23]] season. Haaland's next goal saw him break the record of most goals scored in a season by a foreign player, ending Robledo's 71-year-old record.<ref>{{cite news |title=Haaland breaks single-season goals record |url=http://www.premierleague.com/news/3253961 |date=3 May 2023 |access-date=4 May 2023 |website=Premier League}}</ref> Haaland finished the season with 36 goals, the highest goal amount since [[Ron Davies (footballer, born 1942)|Ron Davies]] scored 37 for [[Southampton F.C.|Southampton]] fifty-eight years ago. However all these totals are dwarfed by the all time record holder, [[Everton F.C.|Everton]] legend [[Dixie Dean]], who still holds the record for the most goals in a season with 60, set in the [[1927–28 Football League First Division|1927–28]] season.<ref>{{cite web |title=Dixie Dean Hall Of Fame Profile |url=https://www.nationalfootballmuseum.com/halloffame/dixie-dean/ |access-date=15 September 2022}}</ref> Dean's 310 goals scored for Everton is still the record for most goals scored for one club, and also still holds the records for most hat-tricks, both overall and in a single season.<ref name=":18">{{Cite web |date=7 April 2020 |title=Dixie Dean |url=https://www.efcstatto.com/tag/dixie-dean/ |access-date=2022-09-17 |website=EFC Statto}}</ref>

Since 2000, only three Englishmen have won the award. In the [[1999–2000 FA Premier League|1999–2000]] season [[Kevin Phillips (footballer)|Kevin Phillips]] won with 30 goals for [[Sunderland A.F.C.|Sunderland]].<ref name=":2" /> This was a record for most goals by a debut player, in a 38 match season, until Erling Haaland broke it in the 2022–23 season. [[Harry Kane]] won the Golden Boot in successive seasons when he scored 25 in [[2015–16 Premier League|2015–16]] and then 29 in the [[2016–17 Premier League|2016–17]] season. He won it again in the [[2020–21 Premier League|2020–21]] season with 23.<ref name=":9" /> The third is [[Jamie Vardy]]; the [[Leicester City F.C.|Leicester City]] striker scored 23 goals in the [[2019–20 Premier League|2019–20]] season.<ref name=":9" />

== Top 50 all-time top scorers ==
[[File:Jimmy Greaves (cropped).jpg|thumb|All time record goal scorer [[Jimmy Greaves]] who scored 357 goals in 516 matches. He is the record holder of top scorer awards with six and record league goalscorer for [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]] still, with 220.]]
The [[Football League First Division|Football League Division One]] from 1888 through to the end of the 1991–92 season and now the [[Premier League]], make up the top tier in English football.&nbsp;During these 137 years three players have scored over 300 goals, with another 25 scoring over 200 goals.&nbsp;A further three players were a goal shy, finishing on 199 goals. The first was [[Sheffield Wednesday F.C.|Sheffield Wednesday's]] [[Andrew Wilson (footballer, born 1879)|Andrew Wilson]]<ref>{{cite web |title=DT92 ~ Andy Wilson |url=http://doingthe92.com/display_player.asp?step=61&ID=38&pid=51158&ptag=Andy_Wilson |access-date=14 September 2022 |website=Doing the 92}}</ref> whose career was interrupted by [[World War I]] but went onto make 501 appearances. In the mid-sixties, [[Bobby Smith (footballer, born 1933)|Bobby Smith]]<ref>{{cite web |title=DT92 ~ Bobby Smith |url=http://www.doingthe92.com/display_player.asp?step=61&ID=49&pid=41913&ptag=Bobby_Smith |access-date=14 September 2022 |website=Doing the 92}}</ref> retired after scoring 23 in 74 for Chelsea and 176 in 271 for Tottenham, and finally ten years later, [[England national football team|England]] legend [[Bobby Charlton|Sir Bobby Charlton]],<ref>{{cite web |title=DT92 ~ Bobby Charlton |url=http://doingthe92.com/display_player.asp?step=80&ID=11&pid=115&ptag=Bobby%20Charlton |access-date=14 September 2022 |website=Doing the 92}}</ref> left Manchester United after making 606 appearances.

[[Derby County F.C.|Derby County]] forward [[Steve Bloomer]] was the first player to score over 300 goals, his record of 314 stood for over half a century.&nbsp;In 14 years, he scored 240 goals in 376 matches in his first stint at Derby County before moving to [[Middlesbrough F.C.|Middlesbrough]] where he scored 59 in 125 games for the Boro.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=DT92 ~ Steve Bloomer |url=http://www.doingthe92.com/display_player.asp?step=61&ID=28&pid=51770&ptag=Steve_Bloomer |access-date=14 September 2022 |website=Doing the 92}}</ref> After five years on Teesside, he returned to Derby who were in the second division then.&nbsp;He spent two years in the second division scoring 38 goals before the Rams won promotion. In his final two seasons he scored a further 15 goals in 34 matches, a total of 255 in 410 appearances for Derby County. [[Everton F.C.|Everton]] striker [[Dixie Dean]] came very close to breaking the record, he scored 349 league goals all for Everton, however 39 were scored in the second division, leaving him 4 goals behind. Bloomers' achievement was finally surpassed when [[Jimmy Greaves]] broke the record scoring 357 goals, playing for [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]], [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]] and [[West Ham United F.C.|West Ham United]].&nbsp;For Chelsea he scored 124 goals in 157 appearances, only [[Frank Lampard]] 147,<ref name=":1">{{cite web |date=11 October 2021 |title=Chelsea top scorers of all time with full details |url=https://interestingfootball.com/chelsea-all-time-top-scorers-in-history-with-full-details/ |access-date=14 September 2022}}</ref> [[Roy Bentley]] 130,<ref name=":1" /> and [[Bobby Tambling]] 129<ref name=":1" /> have scored more top flight goals for Chelsea. Greaves moved on to [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]] where, to this day, remains Tottenham's top league goalscorer after scoring 220 goals in 321 appearances.<ref>{{cite web |title=Jimmy Greaves |url=https://www.tottenhamhotspur.com/the-club/history/legends/jimmy-greaves/ |access-date=14 September 2022 |publisher=Tottenham Hotspur F.C.}}</ref> His top flight career ended at West Ham United, where he scored 13 in 38 matches.<ref>{{cite web |title=DT92 ~ Jimmy Greaves |url=http://www.doingthe92.com/display_player.asp?step=61&ID=19&pid=116&ptag=Jimmy_Greaves |access-date=14 September 2022 |website=Doing the 92}}</ref>

In the [[Premier League]] era, [[Alan Shearer]]<ref name=":2">{{cite web |title=Premier League Player Stats - Goals |url=https://www.premierleague.com/stats/top/players/goals?co=1&se=-1&co=1&cl=-1&iso=-1&po=-1%3Fse%3D-1 |access-date=29 May 2023 |website=Premier League |archive-date=26 June 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200626065900/https://www.premierleague.com/stats/top/players/goals?co=1&se=-1&co=1&cl=-1&iso=-1&po=-1%3Fse%3D-1 |url-status=dead }}</ref> sits top, but even with his full tally of 283 goals, he still trails.&nbsp;Four more "modern day" players, who have played in the Premier League make the list, [[Wayne Rooney]],<ref name=":2" /> the third highest Premier League goalscorer with 208 goals for Everton and [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]], is 22nd. [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] legend [[Ian Rush]]<ref name=":2" /> is the 14th highest scorer in the history of top flight football, but his Premier League tally is only 48 goals, ranking him 144th.&nbsp;Another player to lose goals is [[Tony Cottee]],<ref name=":2" /> who sits in 18th place.&nbsp;His last 78 goals gives him a current PL ranking of 62. Apart from these three, a further 20 players, who have scored 100 or more goals, have lesser totals.&nbsp;Ranked 45th, [[Lee Chapman]]<ref name=":12">{{cite web |title=Lee Chapman |url=https://www.worldfootball.net/person/pe215679/lee-chapman/ |access-date=14 September 2022 |website=WorldFootball.net}}</ref> scored 177 goals, the same as [[Frank Lampard]] and two more than [[Thierry Henry]], but his last 23 goals sees him in 365th place in the Premier League.<ref name=":2" /> [[Peter Beardsley]]<ref name=":13">{{cite web |title=Peter Beardsley {{!}} Football Stats |url=https://www.soccerbase.com/players/player.sd?player_id=522 |access-date=14 September 2022 |website=Soccer Base}}</ref> and [[Matt Le Tissier]]<ref>{{cite web |title=Matt Le Tissier {{!}} Football Stats |url=https://www.soccerbase.com/players/player.sd?player_id=7972 |access-date=14 September 2022 |website=Soccer Base}}</ref> (jointly ranked 71st), both scored 161 goals, 11 more than [[Michael Owen]] who is eleventh on the PL list. Beardsley is in 97th position with 58 goals in the Premier League while a lack of centurions, assists Le Tissier's ranking. Losing 61 goals improves his overall position, ranked 34th in the [[List of footballers with 100 or more Premier League goals|Premier League]] with 100 goals.<ref name=":2" />

The most recent active player in the Top 50 is [[Mohamed Salah]]; his goal against Leicester City on [[Boxing Day|Boxing day]], 2024, was his 173rd, moving the Egyptian winger inside the top 50. Recently, former Tottenham Hotspur striker [[Harry Kane]],<ref name=":2" /> scored 30 goals in his last season in England to move above players such as [[Dennis Viollet]],<ref>{{cite web |title=DT92 ~ Dennis Viollet |url=http://www.doingthe92.com/display_player.asp?step=80&ID=11&pid=98&ptag= |access-date=14 September 2022 |website=Doing the 92}}</ref> [[Ray Charnley]]<ref>{{cite web |title=DT92 ~ Ray Charnley |url=http://www.doingthe92.com/display_player.asp?step=80&ID=36&pid=5812 |access-date=14 September 2022 |website=Doing the 92}}</ref> who both had 190 goals, [[Peter Harris (footballer)|Peter Harris]],<ref>{{cite web |url=https://pompeyrama.com/pompey-fc-players-209-Peter-Harris.html |title=Peter Harris |access-date=17 September 2022 |website=Pompeyrama}}</ref> who scored 192 goals for [[Portsmouth F.C.|Portsmouth]], [[Stan Mortensen]]<ref>{{cite web |title=DT92 ~ Stan Mortensen |url=http://www.doingthe92.com/display_player.asp?step=80&ID=45&pid=33040&ptag=Stan_Mortensen |access-date=14 September 2022 |website=Doing the 92}}</ref> who scored 197 goals for [[Blackpool F.C.|Blackpool]], [[George Elliott (footballer, born 1889)|George Elliott]]<ref>{{cite web |title=DT92 ~ George Elliott |url=http://www.doingthe92.com/display_player.asp?step=490&ID=1&pid=53282 |access-date=14 September 2022 |website=Doing the 92}}</ref> who scored 198 goals for [[Middlesbrough F.C.|Middlesbrough]] and the three players mentioned above who all scored 199 goals. Kane, ranked 19th, became only the 28th player in 136 years of league football to join the elite 200 club, who, in the summer of 2023, signed for German club [[FC Bayern Munich|Bayern Munich]].<ref>{{Cite news |date=2023-08-12 |title=Harry Kane joins Bayern Munich ending record-breaking Tottenham career |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/66484550 |access-date=2024-09-28 |work=BBC Sport}}</ref>

[[Lee Chapman]] holds the record of most top flight clubs scored for with eight. [[Andy Cole]] played for eight clubs also, but only scored for six. [[Marcus Bent]] is another player to play for eight top flight clubs, again only scoring for six.<ref>{{cite web |title=Marcus Bent Forward, Profile & Stats |url=https://www.premierleague.com/players/1382/Marcus-Bent/overview |access-date=31 October 2022 |website=Premier League}}</ref> A name that does not appear on the top scorer list is [[Arthur Rowley]], the record holder for the [[List of footballers in England by number of league goals|most goals in league football]], scoring 434 goals in 619 league games. Arthur's brother [[Jack Rowley]] scored 173 goals for [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]] and is ranked 50th, shown above. Arthur however didn't play much top flight football in his career, but he did score 51 goals in 95 matches. In one season at [[Fulham F.C.|Fulham]] he scored eight in 34 appearances and then later hit 43 in 61 appearances over two seasons for [[Leicester City F.C.|Leicester City]].<ref>{{cite web |title=DT92 ~ Arthur Rowley |url=http://www.doingthe92.com/display_player.asp?step=61&ID=32&pid=10&ptag=Arthur_Rowley |access-date=31 October 2022 |website=Doing the 92}}</ref>

== Club's top scorers in top tier ==
The start of the [[English Football League|Football League]] saw 12 teams become the founding members of the first ever league season in 1888–89. These were [[Accrington Stanley F.C. (1891)|Accrington]], [[Blackburn Rovers F.C.|Blackburn Rovers]], [[Bolton Wanderers F.C.|Bolton Wanderers]], [[Burnley F.C.|Burnley]], [[Everton F.C.|Everton]], [[Preston North End F.C.|Preston North End]], [[Aston Villa F.C.|Aston Villa]], [[Derby County F.C.|Derby County]], [[Notts County F.C.|Notts County]], [[Stoke City F.C.|Stoke City]], [[West Bromwich Albion F.C.|West Bromwich Albion]] and [[Wolverhampton Wanderers F.C.|Wolverhampton Wanderers]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Football League - facts, stats and history |url=https://www.footballhistory.org/league/football-league.html |access-date=26 December 2022 |website=Football History}}</ref> Since then, 65 clubs have played at the top level, with only four [[Premier League]] players breaking club records set in the football league. [[Thierry Henry]] surpassed the 150 goals scored by [[Cliff Bastin]] for [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]].<ref>{{cite web |title=DT92 ~ Cliff Bastin |url=http://www.doingthe92.com/display_player.asp?step=61&ID=1&pid=2689&ptag=Cliff_Bastin |access-date=26 December 2022 |website=Doingthe92}}</ref> [[Roy Bentley]], who scored 130 goals for [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]],<ref name=":1" /> was surpassed by [[Frank Lampard]], while [[Sergio Agüero]] overtook the 147 goals [[Eric Brook]] scored for [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]].<ref>{{cite web |title=DT92 ~ Eric Brook |url=http://doingthe92.com/display_player.asp?step=61&ID=10&pid=46768&ptag=Eric_Brook |access-date=26 December 2022 |website=Doingthe92}}</ref> [[Matt Le Tissier]] scored in both the First Division and the Premier League to become [[Southampton F.C.|Southampton]]'s top scorer, exceeding the 134-goal record set by Welshman [[Ron Davies (footballer, born 1942)|Ron Davies]].<ref>{{cite web |title=DT92 ~ Ron Davies |url=http://www.doingthe92.com/display_player.asp?step=61&ID=74&pid=149&ptag=Ron_Davies |access-date=26 December 2022 |website=www.Doingthe92}}</ref> [[Danny Welbeck]] scored 46 goals for [[Brighton & Hove Albion F.C.|Brighton & Hove Albion]], 9 above previous record holder [[Michael Robinson (footballer)|Michael Robinson]]'s tally of 37. The Premier League's top three goalscorers, who all have scored over 200 goals, fail to appear; [[Alan Shearer]] finished nine goals adrift of [[Blackburn Rovers F.C.|Blackburn]]'s [[Ted Harper]]<ref>{{cite web |title=DT92 ~ Ted Harper |url=http://www.doingthe92.com/display_player.asp?step=490&ID=1&pid=53268 |access-date=26 December 2022 |website=Doingthe92}}</ref> and finished two short of [[Newcastle United F.C.|Newcastle]] legend [[Jackie Milburn]],<ref>{{cite web |title=DT92 ~ Jackie Milburn |url=http://doingthe92.com/display_player.asp?step=61&ID=13&pid=8&ptag=Jackie_Milburn |access-date=26 December 2022 |website=Doingthe92}}</ref> [[Wayne Rooney]] was sixteen short of [[Bobby Charlton]]'s record for [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]], and [[Harry Kane]] departed [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]] with 213 goals, leaving [[Jimmy Greaves]] as the club's record top flight scorer.

[[Glossop North End A.F.C.|Glossop]] statistics currently unavailable.

== Top five scorers by nationality/region ==
[[File:Salah_in_2018.jpg|thumb|
With 193 goals, [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] winger [[Mohamed Salah]] is currently the highest foreign goalscorer in English top flight history.]]
Many nationalities have played in English top flight football throughout the years. The tables below show the top five highest scorers from their respective countries or region. As shown in the top 50 list above, the top English and Scottish goal scorers can be seen.

Of the [[Home Nations|home nation]] countries, players from the Premier League era are well short of the overall records. [[Irish Football Association|Northern Ireland]]'s top scorer is [[Iain Dowie]], who scored 33 of his 57 goals in the Premier League. The top [[Football Association of Wales|Welsh]] goal scorer is [[Ryan Giggs]], who scored 114 goals (109 in the Premier League), while [[Duncan Ferguson]] with 68 goals is the top [[Scottish Football Association|Scottish]] goalscorer in the Premier League. These numbers all fall short of the record top flight totals set by [[Derek Dougan]], [[Ian Rush]] and [[Hughie Gallacher]]. Elsewhere, [[Football Association of Ireland|Republic of Ireland]] striker [[Robbie Keane]] scored 126 goals in the Premier League, but ended with 10 goals less than record holder [[Frank Stapleton]].<ref name=":19" /> 

A different story occurs with the rest of the world, made up predominately of Premier League-era players only. South American [[George Robledo]]'s record remains from the 1950s, and he is currently the joint third-highest South American goalscorer. [[Craig Johnston]] has been overtaken by Premier League [[Oceania Football Confederation|Oceanic]] players, while [[Lindy Delapenha]] also lost his [[Caribbean Football Union|Caribbean]] record. American [[Roy Wegerle]] has dropped to second in the United States and Canada scorers; his goals span the switch to the Premier League. The top European and African scorers are all from the Premier League era.

When [[Dwight Yorke]] scored a hat-trick for [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]] against [[Leicester City F.C.|Leicester City]], on 17 January 1999,<ref>{{cite news |title=FA Carling Premiership {{!}} United smash Foxes |url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/sport/football/fa_carling_premiership/256048.stm |access-date=1 April 2023 |website=BBC Sport}}</ref> he became the league's top foreign scorer. With this treble, he moved onto 84 top flight goals, surpassing the previous record of 82, set by Chilean George Robledo in 1953.<ref>{{cite web |date=5 May 2022 |title=His brother's keeper: remembering George and Ted Robledo |url=https://www.aroundtownmagazine.co.uk/his-brothers-keeper-remembering-george-and-ted-robledo/ |access-date=1 April 2023 |website=AroundTown Magazine}}</ref> Later that year, on 18 December 1999, Yorke scored twice for Manchester United in a 4–2 away win at [[West Ham United F.C.|West Ham United]].<ref>{{cite web |title=FA CARLING PREMIERSHIP {{!}} Man Utd run riot |url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/sport/football/fa_carling_premiership/570990.stm |access-date=1 April 2023 |website=BBC Sport}}</ref> His first goal that day saw him become the first foreign player to score 100 top flight goals in England.<ref>{{cite web |title=ROBLEDO |url=https://inbedwithmaradona.com/journal/2015/2/26/the-innovator-of-iquique-the-story-of-george-robledo |access-date=1 April 2023 |website=IBWM}}</ref> This was his 27th league goal for Manchester United, after scoring 73 previously for [[Aston Villa F.C.|Aston Villa]]. As of 2026, his 136 goals ranks him as the fifth-highest foreign goalscorer, behind [[Mohamed Salah]]'s 193, [[Sergio Agüero]]'s 184, [[Thierry Henry]]'s 175 and [[Robin van Persie]]'s 144.

* '''Bold''' shows players currently playing in the [[Premier League]].

== Players with 100 or more goals ==
[[File:Beardsley, Peter.jpg|thumb|248x248px|[[Peter Beardsley]] scored 161 goals in the first tier: 88 goals for [[Newcastle United F.C.|Newcastle United]], 46 for [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]], 25 for [[Everton F.C.|Everton]] and 2 for [[Bolton Wanderers F.C.|Bolton Wanderers]].]]

As of 2026, a total of 256 players have scored 100 or more goals in the English first tier.<ref name=Free-elements-history>{{cite web |title=Top Division English League Goal Scorers 1888-2026 (201-300) |url=http://www.free-elements.com/England/ts2.html |access-date=2 August 2026 |website=Free-Elements}}</ref> [[Erling Haaland]] in the [[2025–26 Premier League|2025–26 season]] became the latest player to reach a century of goals, all scored for [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Haaland joins the Premier League's 100 Club in record time |url=https://www.premierleague.com/en/news/4455995 |date=2 December 2025 |access-date=2 December 2025 |publisher=Premier League}}</ref>

Starting in 1992–93, the [[Foundation of the Premier League|Premier League]] was established as the first tier English football competition, replacing the [[Football League First Division]]. The Premier League does not include matches prior to its establishment in record-keeping, which has been criticized. In a 2016 interview published in the [[Irish Independent]], former [[Leeds United F.C.|Leeds United]] legend [[Johnny Giles]] stated "What other sport wipes out 100 years of records and standards and decides that [[Alan Shearer]] was the first player to score 100 goals for two clubs when [[Jimmy Greaves]] did it decades before? In no other sport in England is there such a casual disregard and disrespect for the achievements of players who inhabit the archives..."<ref>{{cite web |title=John Giles: Sky didn't invent football and it didn't begin in 1992 either |url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/soccer/premier-league/john-giles-sky-didnt-invent-football-and-it-didnt-begin-in-1992-either/34347385.html |access-date=13 May 2023 |publisher=Irish Independent |date=8 January 2016 }}</ref>

Of the 256 players to score 100 or more goals in the English first tier:<ref name=Free-elements-history/>
*214 players scored 100 or more goals in the [[Football League First Division|First Division]] prior to the 1992–93 season.
*35 players have scored 100 or more goals in the [[Premier League]] since 1992–93.{{efn|See also: [[List of footballers with 100 or more Premier League goals]]}} 
*7 players that scored fewer than 100 goals in either the First Division or the Premier League separately scored 100 or more goals in total in the first tier.

== Player records ==
'''All records listed below pertain to league matches played in Division 1 and/or the Premier League only.'''

Most goals in a season:

* 42 matches – 60 [[Dixie Dean]], Everton 1927–28<ref>{{Cite web |title=Dixie Dean Hall Of Fame Profile |url=https://www.nationalfootballmuseum.com/halloffame/dixie-dean/ |access-date=2022-09-17}}</ref>
* 38 matches – 38 [[Bert Freeman]], Everton 1908–09<ref name=":16">{{cite web|url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablese/engtops.html|title=English League Leading Goalscorers|publisher=[[Rec.Sport.Soccer Statistics Foundation]]|access-date=2010-10-31}}</ref>

Most goals in a debut season:

* 42 matches – 38 [[Dave Halliday]], Sunderland 1925–26<ref>{{Cite web |title=Sunderland AFC - Statistics, History and Records - from TheStatCat |url=http://www.catstattery.co.uk/Season.aspx?SeasonID=47 |access-date=2023-02-18 |website=www.catstattery.co.uk}}</ref>
* 38 matches – 36 [[Erling Haaland]], Manchester City 2022–23<ref name=":6">{{Cite web |title=Haaland equals Salah's 32-goal Premier League record |url=http://www.premierleague.com/news/3152469 |access-date=2023-04-15 |website=www.premierleague.com}}</ref>

Most penalties scored: 56 [[Alan Shearer]] (from 67 taken for Blackburn Rovers and Newcastle United, 1992–2006)<ref>{{Cite web |title=Premier League + 1. Division - All-time best penalty takers |url=https://www.worldfootball.net/alltime_goalgetter/eng-premier-league/elfmeter/1/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141021210737/http://www.worldfootball.net/alltime_goalgetter/eng-premier-league/elfmeter/1/ |url-status=dead |archive-date=21 October 2014 |access-date=2023-05-03 |website=worldfootball.net}}</ref>

Most penalties scored in 1 season: 13 [[Francis Lee (footballer)|Francis Lee]], Manchester City 1971–72<ref>{{Cite web |title=Lee Franny |url=https://www.mancity.com/mancitylegends/lee-franny |access-date=2022-10-15 |website=Manchester City FC}}</ref>

Most consecutive Top Scorer awards: 3

* [[Jimmy Greaves]] (1963, 1964, 1965)
* [[Alan Shearer]] (1995, 1996, 1997)
* [[Thierry Henry]] (2004, 2005, 2006)

Most top scorer awards with different clubs: 3 [[Gary Lineker]] (Leicester City 1985, Everton 1986, Tottenham Hotspur 1990)

100 goals for two clubs: 3<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-07-16 |title=Nostalgia: The record-breaking Bolton football star who boasted many claims to fame |url=https://www.inyourarea.co.uk/news/nostalgia-the-record-breaking-bolton-football-star-who-boasted-many-claims-to-fame/ |access-date=2023-05-03 |website=InYourArea.co.uk}}</ref>

* [[David Jack]] 1919–34 (Bolton Wanderers 144 – Arsenal 113)
* [[Jimmy Greaves]] 1957–1970 (Chelsea 124 – Tottenham Hotspur 220)
* [[Alan Shearer]] 1992–2006 (Blackburn Rovers 112 – Newcastle United 148)

Fastest player to reach 100 goals: [[Dave Halliday]] in 101 games for [[Sunderland A.F.C.|Sunderland]].<ref name="DH">{{cite web|url=http://qosfc.com/content-legendsView.aspx?playerid=1048|title=QosFC: Legends - Dave Halliday|website=qosfc.com}}</ref>

Players to score over 30 league goals in four consecutive seasons: [[Dave Halliday]], 1925–26 to 1928–29.<ref name="DH" /> Halliday scored at least 35 goals in each of those four seasons.<ref name="DH" />
